"""Core task operations. due_at throughout this module is in SECONDS, matching models.Task."""
import time

from tinytasks.models import Task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all, next_id, save_all


def create_task(title: str, due_in_seconds: float) -> Task:
    """Create a task due `due_in_seconds` seconds from now."""
    tasks = load_all()
    task = Task(id=next_id(tasks), title=title, due_at=time.time() + due_in_seconds)
    tasks.append(task)
    save_all(tasks)
    return task


def get_overdue_tasks(now: float | None = None) -> list[Task]:
    """Tasks whose due_at (seconds) has already passed."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    return [t for t in load_all() if t.due_at < now and not t.archived]


def delete_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    tasks = load_all()
    remaining = [t for t in tasks if t.id != task_id]
    save_all(remaining)
    return len(remaining) != len(tasks)


def archive_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    """Soft-delete: mark the task archived and keep its record."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            t.archived = True
            save_all(tasks)
            return True
    return False

import argparse

from tinytasks.api import create_task, delete_task, get_overdue_tasks
from tinytasks.text import normalize_title


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="tinytasks")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_add = sub.add_parser("add")
    p_add.add_argument("title")
    p_add.add_argument("--due-in", type=float, required=True, help="seconds from now")

    sub.add_parser("overdue")

    p_del = sub.add_parser("delete")
    p_del.add_argument("id", type=int)

    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.cmd == "add":
        t = create_task(normalize_title(a.title), a.due_in)
        print(f"created task {t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "overdue":
        for t in get_overdue_tasks():
            print(f"{t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "delete":
        print("deleted" if delete_task(a.id) else "no such task")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from tinytasks.api import archive_task, create_task, get_overdue_tasks
from tinytasks.storage import load_all
from tinytasks.text import normalize_title


def _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TINYTASKS_DATA", str(tmp_path / "data.json"))


def test_archive_task_keeps_record(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("old", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert archive_task(t.id) is True
    assert [x.archived for x in load_all()] == [True]


def test_archive_task_missing_returns_false(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    assert archive_task(999) is False


def test_overdue_skips_archived(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("late", due_in_seconds=-10)
    create_task("late too", due_in_seconds=-10)
    archive_task(t.id)
    assert [x.title for x in get_overdue_tasks()] == ["late too"]


def test_normalize_title():
    assert normalize_title("  a \t b\n\n c  ") == "a b c"
    assert len(normalize_title("x" * 200)) == 80
    assert normalize_title("") == ""


def test_create_task_keeps_raw_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    assert create_task("  raw   title ", 1).title == "  raw   title "

import sys
import time

from tinytasks import cli
from tinytasks.api import clear_overdue, create_task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all


def _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TINYTASKS_DATA", str(tmp_path / "data.json"))


def test_clear_overdue_archives_and_counts(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("late", due_in_seconds=-10)
    create_task("later", due_in_seconds=-5)
    create_task("future", due_in_seconds=3600)
    assert clear_overdue() == 2
    tasks = load_all()
    assert [(t.title, t.archived) for t in tasks] == [
        ("late", True), ("later", True), ("future", False)]
    assert clear_overdue() == 0


def test_cli_clear_overdue_prints_count(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("late", due_in_seconds=-10)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["tinytasks", "clear-overdue"])
    cli.main()
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "1"


def test_cli_quick_add_due_in_24h_and_normalized(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["tinytasks", "quick-add", "  buy   milk "])
    before = time.time()
    cli.main()
    (t,) = load_all()
    assert t.title == "buy milk"
    assert abs(t.due_at - (before + 86400)) < 5
    assert "created task" in capsys.readouterr().out

content.text:
Both commands are added and committed as `16933a5`. The suite passes (11 tests, including 3 new ones in `tests/test_clear_and_quick_add.py`).

- **`clear-overdue`**: `clear_overdue()` in `tinytasks/api.py` returns the number of tasks it removed, and the command prints that number. It archives overdue tasks instead of deleting them, because the team's Plexus memory says new code must not hard-delete tasks. Archived tasks stay in the data file and no longer show up in `overdue`. I left `delete_task` and the `delete` command untouched, as the same convention requires.
- **`quick-add TITLE`**: creates a task due 24 hours from now. The title goes through `normalize_title()` first, which is also a team convention. I didn't normalize inside `create_task`, since the CSV importer relies on raw titles.

The deleted `.pyc` files that were already showing in git status are not part of the commit.
